memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Every grain offering baked in an oven or cooked in a pan or on a griddle belongs to the priest who offers it, and every grain offering, whether mixed with olive oil or dry, belongs equally to all the sons of Aaron.'" - Lev 7:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Some offerings went to the individual priest who handled them. Others were shared equally among all the priests.

That second arrangement is quietly wise. If every priest kept only what he personally received, the ones serving during busy festival weeks would prosper and those on quiet rotations would go hungry. Ministry would become competitive. Priests would jostle for the best shifts.

God built sharing into the system to prevent exactly that.

The early church rediscovered this instinct. All the believers were together and had everything in common... They gave to anyone who had need (Acts 2:44-45). Paul organised a collection from wealthier churches for the struggling believers in Jerusalem, explaining the principle: at the present time your plenty will supply what they need, so that in turn their plenty will supply what you need. The goal is equality (2 Cor 8:14).

This is not a political programme; it is a family instinct. In a healthy household, nobody eats while a sibling starves.

Look around your church, your family, your circle. Is there someone in a lean season while you are in a full one?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I hold what I have as mine alone, or as something available to my brothers and sisters?
2. Who around me is in a lean season right now?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for what You have given me. Show me who I should be sharing it with, and make me willing. Amen.
